records.title: OneDayAgent: Towards a Long-Horizon Harness for Autonomous Agents
records.reason: OneDayAgent provides a long-horizon agent harness for task evaluation; the abstract targets reliability and capability assessment rather than systems throughput, latency, or memory efficiency.

records.title: ShapleyLaw: A Game-Theoretic Approach to Multilingual Scaling Laws
records.reason: ShapleyLaw studies multilingual model scaling and language contribution under training; it does not propose an execution-system optimization.

records.title: CARAT: Client-Side Adaptive RPC and Cache Co-Tuning for Parallel File Systems
records.reason: CARAT co-tunes RPC and caching for parallel file systems, but the abstract targets generic HPC file I/O and establishes no LLM inference/serving connection.

records.title: Evaluating large language models for clinical note processing: local fine-tuning and internal-external validation using electronic health records from South Asia
records.reason: The Springer Nature abstract evaluates local fine-tuning of LLMs for clinical extraction and question answering across EHR datasets; this is a clinical application/generalization study, not an inference-system efficiency contribution.

records.title: Disentangling Geometry, Performance, and Training in Language Models
records.reason: This work analyzes geometry/performance/training relationships in language models but presents no concrete serving, runtime, cache, or inference-efficiency mechanism in the abstract.

records.title: EigenAI: Deterministic Inference, Verifiable Results
records.reason: The arXiv abstract establishes deterministic inference and verifiable results, which touches inference runtime infrastructure, but gives no concrete latency, throughput, memory, or energy improvement; relevance to this efficiency-focused lane remains limited.

records.title: Convergence Rate Analysis of the AdamW-style Shampoo: Unifying One-Sided and Two-Sided Preconditioning
records.reason: The paper analyzes convergence rates for AdamW-style Shampoo optimizers; it concerns training optimization theory rather than LLM inference systems.

records.title: Approximation Capabilities of Feedforward Neural Networks with GELU Activations
records.reason: The paper studies approximation properties of GELU feedforward networks; it does not connect the theory to LLM serving or practical inference efficiency.

records.title: Optimizing Distributed Training in Computing Power Networks: A Heterogeneity-aware Approach
records.reason: The publisher abstract proposes hierarchical synchronization and topology selection to improve distributed training over heterogeneous WAN nodes; it is training efficiency, outside the inference-system focus.

records.title: VariPar: Variation-Aware Workload Partitioning in Chiplet-Based DNN Accelerators
records.reason: The DOI/title identity is supported by available bibliographic records, but the IEEE Xplore landing page/abstract could not be retrieved (DOI resolver inaccessible and publisher search yielded no result). Chiplet workload partitioning could transfer to inference accelerator scheduling, but that connection cannot be assessed from a verified primary abstract.

records.title: A Scalable NorthPole System with End-to-End Vertical Integration for Low-Latency and Energy-Efficient LLM Inference
records.reason: NorthPole integrates hardware and software for low-latency, energy-efficient LLM inference, directly matching inference latency, power, and accelerator-runtime scope.

records.title: EDGC: Entropy-driven Dynamic Gradient Compression for Efficient LLM Training
records.reason: EDGC compresses gradients to reduce communication during LLM training; it does not address inference execution.

records.title: ASAP: an Agentic Solution to Auto-optimize Performance of Large-Scale LLM Training
records.reason: ASAP automatically tunes large-scale LLM training configurations and reports training performance gains; the optimization target is training, not serving/inference.

records.title: Comparison of Vector Database Management Systems for Retrieval Augmented Generation
records.reason: The DOI/title are identifiable, but IEEE Xplore could not be reached (DOI resolver inaccessible; primary publisher search returned no result). Third-party metadata describes vector-database RAG benchmarks, a potentially relevant retrieval-system comparison, but primary abstract verification is missing.

records.title: Measure Before You Manage: Evaluating Agent Working Memory in Coding Agents
records.reason: The arXiv abstract evaluates object-aware compression and retrieval for coding-agent working memory and notes real-system serving limits; this is plausibly related to inference context/memory management, but it reports evaluation rather than a demonstrated serving-efficiency improvement.

records.title: BrainPilot: Automating Brain Discovery with Agentic Research
records.reason: BrainPilot coordinates agents for neuroscience research with evidence graphs and audits; this is a domain application and reliability framework, not a serving-efficiency method.

records.title: NPUsper: Eliminating Redundant Computation for Real-Time Whisper on Mobile NPUs
records.reason: NPUsper removes redundant Whisper decoder work, uses K-step chunk graphs to reduce KV-cache computation and dispatch overhead, and reports latency/TTFT/power reductions on mobile NPUs, directly matching edge-inference systems efficiency.

records.title: Practical Use of Advanced AI Frameworks on Real-Life Scientific Problems: Three Case Studies
records.reason: The bioRxiv study compares autonomous and human-led AI research across scientific case studies; it evaluates agent capability, not LLM runtime or serving efficiency.

records.title: CALIBER: Calibrating Confidence Before and After Reasoning in Language Models
records.reason: CALIBER calibrates pre/post-reasoning confidence and reduces calibration error; its target is answer reliability, not computational efficiency.

records.title: Do Sparse Autoencoders Learn Meaningful Concept Hierarchies?
records.reason: The study proposes an evaluation protocol for sparse-autoencoder feature hierarchies; it concerns interpretability quality, not LLM inference systems.
